第 15 章 Delivering Feedback给出反馈

Jennifer Dyni / 珍妮弗·戴尼

— 第 52 页 —

Delivering feedback—a valuable skill for any team member—is one of those things that has not come naturally to me.

给出反馈——对任何团队成员来说都是一项宝贵技能——是我天生不擅长的事情之一。

I started my career thinking that all it took to be good at sharing appreciations or criticisms was to simply state my perspective out loud. (I'm from Jersey: direct is good.) As it turns out, literally spewing out my thoughts and ideas didn't always go very well—or at least not the way I expected it to. My attempts to help influence up, down, and sideways were rarely sunshine and daisies and much more often eye rolls and terse "sure, whatever" blow offs. I also had some spectacular failures where the things I said quickly led coworkers to get visibly angry and tell me off for my insensitivity to their situation.

刚开始职业生涯时，我以为善于表达欣赏或批评就是把我的观点大声说出来就行。（我来自新泽西：直接就是好的。）事实证明，把想法和观点一股脑倒出来并不总是顺利——至少不总是按我预期的方式。我试图向上、向下、横向施加影响的尝试很少阳光灿烂，更多的是翻白眼和简短的「行吧随便」的敷衍。我还有过一些惨败——我说的话很快让同事明显生气，因为我对他们的处境不够敏感而被训斥。

Clearly, I did a lot of learning what not to do by experiencing it firsthand. To grow as a leader, I've spent a lot of time exploring and trying different tools and techniques that help me deliver feedback more effectively. Following is some of what has helped me become more successful.

显然，我通过亲身经历学到了很多「不要做什么」。为了成长为领导者，我花了很多时间探索和尝试不同的工具和技巧，帮助我更有效地给出反馈。以下是一些帮助我变得更成功的东西。

Start with Frameworks从框架开始

There are many great resources on how to start a conversation with teams or individuals. They map out templates for a variety of situations—for example, appreciation, confrontation, delegation—and I use them to help me map out my opening statement clearly and concisely.

关于如何与团队或个人开启对话，有很多很好的资源。它们为各种情况（比如表达欣赏、面对面对质、授权）提供了模板，我用它们来帮我清晰简明地规划开场白。

One of the frameworks I use often is called "Continue and Consider":

我经常使用的一个框架叫做「继续与考虑」：

  • If I want to help encourage someone or help them recognize a strength, I kick off my discussion with phrases like "keep repeating" or "be confident with more" with [specific thing I see as a strength] and follow up with examples of the behavior or actions I observed personally that I perceive as kicking butt and taking names.如果我想鼓励某人或帮他们认识到自己的优势，我会用「继续保持」或「多自信一点」加上[我看到的具体优势]来开启讨论，然后附上我亲自观察到的、我认为做得很棒的行为或行动的例子。
— 第 53 页 —
  • When I want to help someone recognize a challenge that I feel is holding them back or needs more attention, I use phrases like "consider changing" or "you can improve your effectiveness" [specific thing I see as an area to grow] and then also support that with examples where I've observed them struggle.当我想帮某人认识到我认为阻碍他们或需要更多关注的挑战时，我会用「考虑改变」或「你可以提高效率」加上[我看到的具体成长领域]，然后附上我观察到他们在哪些方面挣扎的例子来支撑。
  • I also try to include a question after my statements, so that I'm inviting the person to respond and we start a conversation about how things might go differently moving forward.我还会在陈述后加一个问题，这样我是在邀请对方回应，我们开始讨论以后怎么才能做得不一样。

The start of a "continue" discussion might look like this:

一个「继续」讨论的开头可能是这样的：

Hey, Ryan. I wanted to give you some feedback about the UI code review you led yesterday with our team. I hope you continue to take the initiative to help our team own the quality of our code, including walking through how to use tools to assess code complexity and run analyses on test coverage. I appreciate that you helped the team walk through refactoring recent UI pull requests without calling out names, helping the team learn without making individuals, especially some of our junior developers, feel bad. How did you think it went?

嘿，Ryan。我想给你一些关于昨天你带领团队做的 UI 代码评审的反馈。希望你继续主动帮助团队把控代码质量，包括带大家怎么用工具评估代码复杂度和分析测试覆盖率。我很欣赏你帮团队过了最近的 UI 重构 PR 而没有点名，帮团队学习而不让个人——尤其是一些初级开发——感到难堪。你觉得怎么样？

A "consider" conversation might begin like:

一个「考虑」对话可能这样开始：

Hannah, I wanted to give you some feedback about the component you've been building for our new feature. When the component was pulled into testing, I noticed that it wasn't integrating shared design libraries and now it will need to be reworked. Consider changing your story analysis process to research or get feedback from other team members about what you might be able to reuse before you start coding.

Hannah，我想给你一些关于你在为新功能做的组件的反馈。组件被拉去测试时，我注意到它没有整合共享设计库，现在需要返工。考虑改变你的故事分析流程——在开始写代码之前，先研究或从其他团队成员那里获取关于你可以复用什么的反馈。

Some other resources I keep going back to if I'm looking for phrases or questions to reach out with feedback include the following:

如果我在找表达反馈的措辞或问题，我经常参考的其他资源包括：

  • Susan Scott's Fierce ConversationsSusan Scott 的《Fierce Conversations》
  • Lyssa Adkin's Coaching Agile TeamsLyssa Adkins 的《Coaching Agile Teams》
  • Kerry Patterson and Joseph Grenny's Crucial ConversationsKerry Patterson 和 Joseph Grenny 的《Crucial Conversations》

Attune with Improv用即兴表演来调谐

The nonverbal cues I'm communicating during conversations are just as important as the words.

我在对话中传达的非语言线索和语言本身一样重要。

To help me recognize when my natural style might not support my message, I've learned a lot about attuning my delivery as well as my listening with improv techniques. I like using the game "Mirror, Mirror" to stretch my powers of detection and reflection. I find an improv buddy, and then we take turns practicing with different scenarios (from happy situations like winning the lottery to frustrating events like losing our keys) and mirroring the eye contact, hand gestures, and facial expressions our improv buddy is communicating. We then debrief on what we saw—what groups of positive or negative signals we used to interpret what the other person's point of view is and how open or closed they are to the conversation.

为了帮我认识到自己的自然风格什么时候可能不支持我的信息，我学了很多用即兴表演技巧来调谐表达和倾听的方法。我喜欢用「镜子，镜子」这个游戏来锻炼我的觉察和反射能力。我找一个即兴搭档，然后我们轮流练习不同场景（从中奖的快乐场景到丢钥匙的沮丧场景），模仿搭档传达的眼神接触、手势和面部表情。然后我们复盘看到了什么——我们用哪些正面或负面信号来解读对方的观点、他们对对话有多开放或封闭。

— 第 54 页 —

Follow Up跟进

There's no such thing as a silver bullet, single perfect feedback conversation. When I'm asking someone to change—even when that change is to do more of a good thing—people often need time to process. I do my best to make it easy for team members to have multiple follow up conversations where they can ask deeper questions about what's expected. What's the urgency? What training or tools do they need? Who else can they connect with for coaching or mentoring? Making myself available to others might look like scheduled or impromptu one on one meetings. Grabbing coffee. A walk around our office campus.

没有银弹，没有一次完美的反馈对话。当我要求某人改变时——即使那个改变是多做好事——人们通常需要时间来消化。我尽量让团队成员方便地进行多次跟进对话，在对话中他们可以问关于期望的更深入问题。紧迫程度如何？他们需要什么培训或工具？他们还可以找谁获得辅导或指导？让自己对他人可用可能表现为定期或即兴的一对一会议。一起喝杯咖啡。在办公园区里散个步。

The Results结果

These tools and techniques have definitely propelled me along my professional journey, helping me progress in my career from individual contributor, to sometimes project/people leader, to full-time engineering team owner. I'm less likely to open mouth, insert foot, especially when I take time to try new techniques in a safe environment. For example, although it seems silly to practice a framework, it helps to role play and try it out a few times so that when you need to use it to start a conversation at work, the word choices feel and sound natural, not scripted (in comparison, try using the "exactly by the template" word choice next time you give feedback to your significant other, who will likely then totally call out that you're clearly up to something).

这些工具和技巧确实推动了我的职业旅程，帮我从独立贡献者，到有时的项目/人员负责人，到全职工程团队负责人，一步步发展。我更不容易祸从口出了，尤其是在我花时间在安全环境中尝试新技巧之后。例如，虽然练习一个框架看起来很傻，但角色扮演试几次是有帮助的，这样当你需要在工作中用它开启对话时，措辞感觉和听起来都自然，不像背稿子（相比之下，下次你给另一半反馈时试试「完全按模板」的措辞，对方很可能会直接拆穿你明显在搞什么鬼）。
